requirements.requirement: The system must compute a specialty match score between 0.0 and 1.0 for each provider based on user-requested specialty input.
The system must assign the highest weight to exact matches between user-requested specialty terms and provider NUCC taxonomy descriptions.
The system must assign a lower weight to partial matches where user terms partially overlap with NUCC taxonomy descriptions.
The system must assign the lowest non-zero weight to inferred matches derived from vector-based semantic similarity.
The system must integrate both regex-based and vector-based matching outputs into a unified scoring calculation.
The system must normalize all computed scores to ensure the final score does not exceed 1.0.
The system must return a score of 0.0 when no regex or vector matches are found.
The system must support multiple NUCC taxonomy codes per provider and aggregate their contributions into a single score.
The system must prioritize the highest scoring NUCC match when multiple matches exist for a provider.
The system must produce intermediate scoring components (exact, partial, inferred) to support downstream explanation generation.
The system must handle user input containing multiple specialties or conditions and compute a composite score.
The system must use the existing specialty_service dual-pipeline (regex + vector) without removing or bypassing either method.
The system must return consistent scores for identical inputs across repeated executions.
The system must handle empty or null user specialty input by returning a score of 0.0 and no matches.
The system must handle malformed or non-string user input by safely defaulting to a score of 0.0 without throwing an unhandled exception.
The system must ensure scoring execution completes within acceptable latency for synchronous evaluation workflows.
